subject: Re: Kickoff: grasping benchmark revival (dql_grasping)
body:
Status on the small-scale comparisons.

On the easy-tier environment with random-policy bootstrap data, early numbers: DQL reaches 78% grasp success, plain MC returns trail at 71% but are the most stable across seeds, DDPG is sample-efficient early then plateaus at 74%, and supervised is the floor at 66%. Corr-MC with eligibility traces is the interesting one — the biased-returns trick from the paper closes most of the MC-vs-DQL gap on the medium tier. PCL still has a divergence issue Quentin is chasing; likely a learning-rate interaction with our ported replay buffer.

Risk for the June sweep: sim throughput. Nikhil's port is functionally done but we're at about 60% of the frames/sec we budgeted, renderer-side. If we can't close it by June 12, the grid needs a trim — I'd cut the hardest difficulty tier before cutting seeds; five seeds is the minimum for the readout to mean anything.

Efe
